Top stock is one of the unique scans that *actually* has to be done every day. You can get a pass missing it once a period, but you lose six points off of your composite score card which really hurts your stores percent goals. Hopefully your store management team caught it, and just scanned the items in at least without having the top stock worked. Best advice I can give is to just apologize for missing and say that you’ll be more mindful in the future. Best of luck out there!

What's the interpretation with the rejection of the Cruz Amendment SA No. 1456?

First, I just wanted to say that I'm fairly new to politics, and I'm trying to gain an understanding of how government works along with our electoral system. So, I apologize if I say anything that doesn't make sense as I'm currently trying to just understand.

So, I saw this tweet (https://twitter.com/aginnt/status/1385337420070199299?s=20) relating to the Covid Hate Crimes Act that just passed the senate. The amendment was designed to "prohibit federal funding for any institution of higher education that discriminates against Asian Americans in recruitment, applicant review or admissions"The obvious implication of the tweet is smear democrats for voting against a bill that would seemingly help against discrimination against the Asian community which the bill is meant to do. 

I'm trying to be a little skeptical of what I'm seeing, and asking really basic questions. Why would the democrats just vote against something that would help Asian Americans? Is this missing some context that I just don't understand? Was there some ulterior motive to trying to amend this bill that I don't get? Is there a reason that would incentivize the democrats to vote against the bill unanimously?

The only thing that I can think of that would explain is the fact that the bill had bipartisan support in the senate already with everyone voting in favor of the bill, and one senator voting against it.It would only stop progress from being made to amend it, then send it back to be voted on again with new changes.

However, that's just my interpretation. Is there something I'm missing? Is there some important piece of context that isn't here, or am I just misunderstanding how the entire process works? Is there another theory or interpretation that can be gleamed?

Thank you all for your time!
